LanguageData.RC2_RawApples.label: apples
LanguageData.RC2_RawApples.description: Raw apples. Tasty red/yellow fruit with a sweet and mildly sour bite to them. Juicy and crisp!
LanguageData.RC2_RawAsparagus.label: asparagus
LanguageData.RC2_RawAsparagus.description: Raw asparagus. These young stalks are harvested before they become too woody to eat. They have a pungeant bite to them.
LanguageData.RC2_RawBanana.label: bananas
LanguageData.RC2_RawBanana.description: Raw bananas. Tasty yellow fruit found in bunches and often used as a form of measurement.
LanguageData.RC2_RawBarley.label: barley
LanguageData.RC2_RawBarley.description: Raw barley. This hardy grain is used in flour and soups, but is also the prime ingredient in beer.
LanguageData.RC2_RawBeets.label: beets
LanguageData.RC2_RawBeets.description: Raw beets. Everything from the root to the leaves are tasty and edible.
LanguageData.RC2_RawBreadfruit.label: breadfruit
LanguageData.RC2_RawBreadfruit.description: Raw breadfruit. A tropical fruit that is known to taste like freshly baked bread or potato.
LanguageData.RC2_RawCabbages.label: cabbages
LanguageData.RC2_RawCabbages.description: Raw cabbages. Great in a variety of dishes, but relatively bland by itself.
LanguageData.RC2_RawCactusFruit.label: cactus fruit
LanguageData.RC2_RawCactusFruit.description: Raw cactus fruits. Make sure to peel the skins before eating them!
LanguageData.RC2_RawCarrots.label: carrots
LanguageData.RC2_RawCarrots.description: Raw carrots. Great in a variety of dishes, and healthy too!
LanguageData.RC2_RawCherries.label: cherries
LanguageData.RC2_RawCherries.description: Raw cherries. These tart fruits have a large seed in them, but are a favorite in wine, desserts, and just eating plain.
LanguageData.RC2_RawChickpeas.label: chickpeas
LanguageData.RC2_RawChickpeas.description: Raw chickpeas. Legumes high in protein that make great hummus!
LanguageData.RC2_RawCocoaBeans.label: cocoa beans
LanguageData.RC2_RawCoconut.label: coconuts
LanguageData.RC2_RawCoconut.description: Raw coconuts. Clanging them together has been known to increase walking speed.
LanguageData.RC2_RawCoffeeBeans.label: coffee beans
LanguageData.RC2_RawCucumbers.label: cucumbers
LanguageData.RC2_RawCucumbers.description: Cucumbers are a gourd plant most well known for making both delicious (Sweet) and gross (Dill) pickles. They can also be eaten raw, but who really does that?
LanguageData.RC2_RawDurians.label: durians
LanguageData.RC2_RawDurians.description: Raw Durians. Some say it smells and tastes like rotten garbage and chemicals. Others find it delicious.
LanguageData.RC2_RawEggplants.label: eggplants
LanguageData.RC2_RawEggplants.description: Raw eggplants. Used in a variety of dishes. Technically they're a fruit, but culinarily they're used as a vegetable.
LanguageData.RC2_RawFigs.label: figs
LanguageData.RC2_RawFigs.description: Raw figs. Delicious right off the tree, Figs are used in a number of delicious meals.
LanguageData.RC2_RawGrapes.label: grapes
LanguageData.RC2_RawGrapes.description: Assorted grapes. Tasty raw but best used in wine making!
LanguageData.RC2_RawJuniperBerries.label: juniper berries
LanguageData.RC2_RawJuniperBerries.description: Fresh Juniper Berries. Not very tasty, but edible. Mostly used in making Gin.
LanguageData.RC2_RawMelons.label: melons
LanguageData.RC2_RawMelons.description: Raw melons. Big, juicy and tasty, these melons are great on a hot summer day.
LanguageData.RC2_RawOats.label: oats
LanguageData.RC2_RawOats.description: Raw oats. Great for cooking, baking, and snacks!
LanguageData.RC2_RawOnion.label: onions
LanguageData.RC2_RawOnion.description: Raw onions. Tasty, smelly bulbs whose layers are peeled. Great with butter.
LanguageData.RC2_RawOrange.label: citrus fruits
LanguageData.RC2_RawOrange.description: Raw citrus fruits. Great for warding off scurvy!
LanguageData.RC2_RawPeaches.label: peaches
LanguageData.RC2_RawPeaches.description: Raw peaches. These dusty-looking fruits have a large pit in the center and are often used to make tea or other stuff.
LanguageData.RC2_RawPecans.label: pecans
LanguageData.RC2_RawPecans.description: Raw pecans. Technically the seed of a fruit, these delicious nutty-like morsels are a great addition to desserts.
LanguageData.RC2_RawPeppers.label: chili peppers
LanguageData.RC2_RawPeppers.description: Raw chili peppers. Hot'n'spicy! Unlike most vegetables, they're good raw or cooked.
LanguageData.RC2_RawPineapples.label: pineapples
LanguageData.RC2_RawPineapples.description: Raw pineapples. A tropical fruit that grows on short plants. It has sweet flesh that is often savored raw by cutting off the top and picking it apart.
LanguageData.RC2_RawPlums.label: plums
LanguageData.RC2_RawPlums.description: Raw plums. These dusty-looking fruits have a large pit in the center and their juice is a favorite of old people.
LanguageData.RC2_RawPomegranates.label: pomegranates
LanguageData.RC2_RawPomegranates.description: Raw pomegranates. Delicious right off the tree, Figs are used in a number of delicious meals.
LanguageData.RC2_RawPumpkins.label: pumpkins
LanguageData.RC2_RawPumpkins.description: Raw pumpkins. Big, juicy and tasty, these pumpkins are great during the autumn.
LanguageData.RC2_RawQuinoa.label: quinoa
LanguageData.RC2_RawQuinoa.description: Raw quinoa. This exotic, rice-like substance is prized for its healthy qualities. Or so the experts would say. They know best, right?
LanguageData.RC2_RawSnapPeas.label: snap peas
LanguageData.RC2_RawSnapPeas.description: Raw snap peas. One of the few vegetables tasty right off the plant. Although technically it's a fruit, but don't tell the chefs that.
LanguageData.RC2_RawSorghum.label: sorghum
LanguageData.RC2_RawSorghum.description: Raw Sorghum. This healthy grain can be cooked similar to rice, or ground up into flour.
LanguageData.RC2_RawSoybean.label: soybeans
LanguageData.RC2_RawSoybean.description: Raw soybeans. Used in soup and dishes, but also turned into a meat substitute.
LanguageData.RC2_RawSugarBeets.label: sugar beets
LanguageData.RC2_RawSugarBeets.description: Raw sugar beets. Edible, but generally too sweet and odd tasting. Better cooked or used to make beet sugar.
LanguageData.RC2_RawSugarcane.label: sugarcane
LanguageData.RC2_RawSugarcane.description: Raw sugarcane. Although you can suck on it to get some of the sweet juices out, its not technically edible.
LanguageData.RC2_RawTeaLeaves.label: tea leaves
LanguageData.RC2_RawTeaLeaves.description: Unfermented Tea Leaves. Used in making relaxing green tea.
LanguageData.RC2_RawTomato.label: tomatoes
LanguageData.RC2_RawTruffles.label: truffles
LanguageData.RC2_RawTruffles.description: Raw truffles. Greatly favored by traders due to its rarity and taste.
LanguageData.RC2_RawWheat.label: wheat grains
LanguageData.RC2_RawWheat.description: Raw wheat grains. Non-edible by humans raw, they must instead be processed and cooked.
LanguageData.RC2_RawYams.label: yams
LanguageData.RC2_RawYams.description: Raw yams. A delicious, filling tuber!
